items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I met her the last two days of the trip you know, and we hit it off and here I am again after three and a half years. But she’s a physicist. She’s an engineer. ... with Leonard Feather and all the Ellington guys on there.

ctx.x: When was your first attempt at putting your own band together? When did that come about?

Well during my time with Ellington, before that, when I stayed at Tizol’s house, they always used to tell me about Pearl, Pearl Bailey. Because she was good friends with the Tizols and she occupied a room in the house also. And I heard, I said “yes, I’ve heard of her,” you know. They said “well you two must meet.” So we finally met in D.C. at the Howard Theater. And that was in ‘51. And after four days, after I met her four days we decided to get married. And that’s, we got married in London, mainly because that…

was a big shock to all of us, you know I thought well I’m going to play my drums and no more, just straight ahead and here I get another blessing. Three and a half years ago I met Francine on a wonderful cruise that you fly up to Vancouver and come back on the cruise you know, with Leonard Feather and all the Ellington guys on there. And I met her the last two days of the trip you know, and we hit it off and here I am again after three and a half years. But she’s a physicist. She’s an engineer.

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Leonard Feather called it the Ellington cruise... I had to tell Leonard Feather, 'I can’t make it.' He said, 'You got to make it.'

ctx.x: Let’s talk about the other great influence in your life, since you brought her up: Francine. When did you meet Francine? How did you come together?

On a cruise. This was a cruise that started in L.A., went up to Vancouver, British Columbia, and back to L.A. Leonard Feather called it the Ellington cruise. Most of the guys – Buster Cooper was on it. If fact Buster Cooper’s the one that introduced me to Francine. The cruise was in October – some time in October – and I had to tell Leonard Feather, “I can’t make it. I got a date booked already at that time.” He said, “You got to make it.” I said, “Let me call up these people I’m supposed to – see if I can cancel…
